title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Set for Marvel's Biggest India Opening Since Avengers: Endgame
excerpt: With 200,000-plus tickets already sold and ₹15 crore in weekend pre-sales, Tom Holland's fourth Spider-Man outing is projected to open at ₹45-50 crore on July 31.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Spider-Man: Brand New Day has sold over 200,000 advance tickets in India with ₹15 crore in pre-sales.
  • Projected opening day earnings of ₹45-50 crore could set a new record for Hollywood in India.
  • PVR-INOX has sold 76,000 first-day tickets worth ₹4 crore, with premium formats nearly sold out.
  • The film will release in six languages, reflecting Hollywood's engagement with India's regional markets.

  • Spider-Man: Brand New Day has sold over 200,000 advance tickets in India with ₹15 crore in opening-weekend pre-sales, 12 days before its July 31 release
  • Projections suggest a ₹45-50 crore opening day, which would make it the biggest Hollywood debut in India since the post-COVID era, potentially surpassing Avatar: The Way of Water's ₹41 crore
  • PVR-INOX alone has sold 76,000 first-day tickets worth ₹4 crore, with premium formats at venues like Prasads in Hyderabad already sold out
  • The film releases in six languages — English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada — across multiple premium formats

Tom Holland's return as Spider-Man is shaping up to be one of the biggest box-office events in Indian cinema history. With nearly two weeks still to go before its July 31 release, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has already amassed over ₹15 crore in advance bookings for its opening weekend and sold more than 200,000 tickets across India.

The numbers suggest a thunderous opening-day collection of ₹45-50 crore net — a figure that would smash Spider-Man: No Way Home's ₹32.67 crore debut from 2021 and potentially eclipse Avatar: The Way of Water's ₹41 crore to become the biggest Hollywood opening in India since the COVID-19 pandemic.

Pre-Sales Breaking Records

The advance booking data reveals the scale of the anticipation. PVR-INOX, India's largest multiplex chain, has sold 76,000 first-day tickets worth ₹4 crore and over 200,000 weekend tickets totalling ₹11.5 crore. Cinepolis has added another 14,000 first-day tickets. BookMyShow, India's leading ticketing platform, processed 44,000 ticket sales on the day standard-format bookings opened and has sold nearly 175,000 tickets total.

Premium properties are already showing sold-out signs. Prasads in Hyderabad — one of India's most iconic cinema halls — is completely booked for opening day and nearly sold out for the rest of the weekend. Several premium large-format screens remain unavailable for Spider-Man, having been reserved for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey under a three-week IMAX exclusivity deal.

India's Marvel Appetite

The pre-sales place Spider-Man: Brand New Day behind only one Marvel film in Indian opening-day history: Avengers: Endgame, which collected ₹53.10 crore in 2019. It will comfortably surpass Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (₹27.5 crore) and Spider-Man: No Way Home (₹32.67 crore) by a wide margin.

The film's six-language release strategy — English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada — reflects Hollywood's deepening engagement with India's regional markets. The available formats span 2D, 4DX 3D, 3D ScreenX, Dolby Cinema, ICE 3D, MX4D, P[XL], and BigPix, covering virtually every premium cinema experience available in the country.

What's Driving the Frenzy

Spider-Man occupies a unique position in India's superhero landscape. The character's fan base spans age groups in a way few Western franchises can match, and the four-year gap since No Way Home has built substantial pent-up demand. The MCU connection amplifies the draw, though Spider-Man's solo box-office performance in India has consistently outpaced other Marvel standalone titles.

Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, Brand New Day reunites Holland with Zendaya and brings the franchise into a new narrative arc. While plot details remain closely guarded, the marketing campaign has generated sustained social media engagement that is translating directly into ticket sales.

The film arrives in a crowded July market — Dhamaal 4 is still running strong and The Odyssey continues to dominate premium screens — but early indicators suggest Spider-Man will carve its own space. For India's multiplex chains, the back-to-back Hollywood and Bollywood blockbusters represent the kind of sustained audience interest that drives the industry's expansion into smaller cities.
